static_traits.name: Hai Li
static_traits.family_status: Living with two turtles; parents divorced
static_traits.social_status: Has several close friends, but the relationship is affected by avoiding talking about career aspirations; has not yet fully shared the extent of anxiety with friends
static_traits.medical_history: Without significant physical illness; without prior psychotherapy history; such psychological problems have not yet occurred before
static_traits.language_features: Clear expression, good logic; neutral tone; able to describe anxiety and avoidance experiences; prone to self-denial when comparing with others

basic_info.main_problem: Believing she will fail on the video game design career path because she cannot code, producing doubt and anxiety.
basic_info.core_demands: Realizes fear of failure is hindering them from pursuing their passion; hopes to deal with these feelings through counseling.
growth_experiences: About two years ago she became interested in video game design, while developing doubt and anxiety from comparing her coding ability with others in the field; over time, fearing failure she avoided opportunities related to game design, and repeatedly felt triggered anxiety when thinking about pursuing the career or seeing others' achievements, affecting academic focus, sleep, and appetite.

Once designed a level and let a friend playtest it; the friend's feedback was that the level was 'very interesting, with great visual effects'; this positive feedback made her briefly feel confident and satisfied.
Learning experience with painting skills: initially poor, but gradually improved through persistent practice, demonstrating the experience that persistence brings progress.

core_beliefs: I am not good enough / not capable of succeeding

special_situations.event: Whenever thinking about pursuing video game design as a career
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I cannot code well, I will definitely fail; better not to try
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Avoiding opportunities related to game design, seeking comfort from friends to relieve anxiety
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I will definitely fail because I cannot code

special_situations.event: When seeing others' achievements or works in this field
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If others are already excellent while I am still no good, it means I can never catch up with them
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Constantly comparing with others, reducing communication and showcasing to avoid being judged
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I am not as good as them; I can never catch up

special_situations.event: When encountering coding difficulties and getting stuck in online tutorials or courses
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Once I feel frustrated with coding, it proves I am not suited for this field
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Interrupting practice, choosing to give up to temporarily reduce anxiety
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I am not suited for coding, which means I cannot do game design

special_situations.event: After receiving positive feedback from friends on level design
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I cannot code, no amount of good design is meaningful
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Negating positive feedback, focusing only on shortcomings
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: This does not matter, because I cannot code

core_conflict.wish: Longs to be recognized and succeed in the video game design field
core_conflict.fear: Fearing failure and being negated, worrying about being unable to handle coding and thus losing worth
defense_goal: Lowering expectations through avoidance and self-denial, maintaining a sense of safety and avoiding further frustration

object_relations.object_representation: Others (peers and high achievers in the field) are strict judges and high-standard competitors

object_relations.self_representation: A creative designer not recognized by herself
object_relations.object_representation: Friends are givers of support and positive feedback

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When others (such as the counselor or friends) emphasize her design strengths or give positive feedback
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Subconsciously treating praise as 'not counting', believing that lacking coding ability will undo all strengths
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Downplaying or denying positive feedback, in a hesitant tone, repeatedly emphasizing 'I cannot code', thus dragging the topic back to flaws.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When encountering difficulties or getting stuck in coding practice
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Interpreting one setback as overall unsuitability, believing continued effort has no meaning
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Using 'I am naturally unsuited for coding''doing this is unrealistic' as reasons to stop practicing, in a rational tone tinged with giving up.

manifestations: Tying personal worth almost entirely to coding ability, negating strengths in design
Still believing 'without coding everything is meaningless' even after receiving positive feedback

contact_model.definition: The individual has a poor capacity for self-reflection and introspection, with excessive self-restriction and self-blame, and is overly cautious about contact, corresponding to 'autonomy'.
manifestations: Excessive comparison and self-denial (believing she can never catch up with others)
Self-limits out of fear of failure, reducing challenges and showing
Still emphasizing her own shortcomings despite positive feedback

contact_model.definition: The individual ignores or avoids a stimulus from the internal or external environment, deliberately avoiding direct contact, corresponding to 'acceptance'.
manifestations: Avoids discussing career aspirations with friends
Turning to giving up or stopping practice when coding anxiety rises, to avoid discomfort

exception_events.target_problem: When letting friends see her work or talking about careers, the client usually avoids or preemptively negates herself, worrying about being judged for not being able to code.
exception_events.unique_outcome: Once she let friends playtest a level she had designed, and the friends responded 'very fun, the visuals are great'; she felt recognized and satisfied at the moment.
exception_events.reason: Clue: different approach - actively sharing and letting friends actually try it; different support: receiving friends' positive feedback; different understanding: briefly noticing her design strengths.

exception_events.target_problem: When facing coding learning, the client usually feels rising anxiety after encountering difficulties and gives up, believing she is not suited for learning new skills.
exception_events.unique_outcome: Unique outcome: in her painting learning experience, she went from 'very poor' at first to gradually improving through practice, proving she can make progress on difficult skills.
exception_events.reason: Clue: different understanding - persistent practice as the path; different approach - sustained training and gradual accumulation; this experience provides replicable clues for subsequent skill acquisition.

positive_force: Has a stable interest and creativity in game design (character and level design)
Has the experience of persisting in practice and making progress (improved painting skills)
Has some social support (several close friends and positive feedback)
Has proactively tried learning coding online (tutorials/courses)
negative_force: Catastrophizing and black-and-white thinking lead to failure anticipation
Comparison and despair tie self-worth almost entirely to others' achievements
Negating positive feedback, focusing only on shortcomings (mental filtering)
Avoiding career-related opportunities, seeking external comfort but finding anxiety hard to relieve

target_behavior.behavior: Avoiding opportunities related to video game design
antecedent: When thinking about doing video game design
When seeing others' achievements or works in the field
When encountering difficulties and getting stuck in coding practice

target_behavior.function: Escaping potential failure and the ensuing anxiety and self-denial
target_behavior.consequence: Skill development and career exploration blocked, work not shown, interpersonal interaction affected (avoiding talking about aspirations)

target_behavior.behavior: Anxiety leads to academic difficulty concentrating
antecedent: When studying, thinks about career choices and coding ability
Encountering coding tasks or related content
target_behavior.core_reason: Emotional reasoning (treating anxious feelings as fact of unsuitability) and fear of failure
target_behavior.function: Briefly reducing discomfort, avoiding difficult tasks
target_behavior.consequence: Declining academic functioning, learning efficiency affected

target_behavior.behavior: Sleep and appetite disturbed (physical manifestations of anxiety)
antecedent: Persistent anxiety triggered when thinking about pursuing video game design or seeing others' achievements
target_behavior.core_reason: Persistent anxiety and worry lead to physiological arousal and stress responses
target_behavior.function: Without obvious external gain function, but sustaining focus on the problem and further weakening daily recovery
target_behavior.consequence: Physical and mental energy declines, further affecting the ability to learn and practice coding
